Check that spicy() is calibrated on your data by shuffling the condition

Source: R/calibrationCheck.R
calibrationCheck.Rd

Shuffles the condition across patients (or across images, without subject), which removes any real difference between the groups while keeping everything else about the study, and runs spicy() on each shuffle. If the test is calibrated, about 5% of pairs have p < 0.05 and about 1% p < 0.01 in each shuffle. Pairs share cells, so the percentage moves by a few points from one shuffle to the next; look at the average over shuffles.

Usage

calibrationCheck(
  cells,
  condition,
  subject = NULL,
  nShuffles = 10,
  thresholds = c(0.05, 0.01),
  ...
)

Arguments

cells

The cells, as for spicy(): a SpatialExperiment, SingleCellExperiment or data.frame (not a store).

condition

The column of the condition to shuffle (a factor, character or Surv column).

subject

The column of the patient. Each patient keeps one condition, moved as a whole; without it, the condition is shuffled across images.

nShuffles

The number of shuffles.

thresholds

The p-value thresholds to report.

...

Other arguments of spicy(), such as r, imageID, cellType or covariates.

Value

A data.frame with one row per shuffle and threshold: shuffle, threshold and percent, the percentage of pairs whose p-value is below the threshold.

Examples

data("diabetesData")
set.seed(1)
calibrationCheck(diabetesData, condition = "stage", subject = "case", r = 50, nShuffles = 2)
#>   shuffle threshold   percent
#> 1       1      0.05 1.7937220
#> 2       1      0.01 0.0000000
#> 3       2      0.05 0.5050505
#> 4       2      0.01 0.0000000
